g.text: C216 · Photodetectors: germanium and the state of the art (§1.4.3)

text.style: font-size: 9.5px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #a1a1a6

g.text: At telecom wavelengths a detector needs a material with a narrower bandgap than silicon — germanium (or bonded III/V) placed on the waveguide.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 10.5px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #f6f6f6

g.text: 1 · Why silicon cannot detect the light

text.style: font-size: 8.5px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #a1a1a6

g.text: a material only absorbs light if its bandgap is narrow enough

g.text: Takeaway: a Si chip needs a narrower-bandgap absorber, so a small Ge (or III/V) detector sits on the waveguide — small means low capacitance and high speed.
